prompt:
Write a node:test regression suite at exactly test/policy.test.js for the existing correct canAccess implementation in src/policy.js. Only create/edit that test file; do not modify production source, existing tests, or package configuration. The suite must pass on the supplied implementation and detect each of these independent policy regressions: accepting anonymous public reads, ignoring suspension, letting administrators cross organizations, ignoring explicit user denials, accepting unknown actions, allowing archived writes, denying an owner's delete, exposing private resources to nonowners, allowing editors to delete other users' resources, and allowing viewers to write. Tests must exercise the imported function with assertions; do not inspect source text or execution environment, replace the implementation, or condition behavior on which version is installed.

Full policy: canAccess(subject, resource, action) returns a boolean without mutating arguments. A null subject is always denied, even for public resources. Any suspended subject is denied. subject.orgId must equal resource.orgId for everyone, including administrators and owners. Membership in resource.deniedUserIds denies every action, even for administrators/owners. The only recognized actions are 'read', 'write', and 'delete'; all other strings are denied for everyone. An archived resource permits only 'read', still subject to all remaining rules. After these gates, a role 'admin' or a subject whose id equals resource.ownerId may do any remaining recognized action, including on private resources. For all other subjects, visibility 'private' denies all access. On 'team' and 'public' resources, both 'viewer' and 'editor' may read; only 'editor' may write; neither may delete. Public visibility never bypasses authentication, organization, explicit denial, suspension, or archive gates.

Subject fields: id, orgId, role ('admin'|'editor'|'viewer'), optional suspended (missing means false). Resource fields: id, orgId, ownerId, visibility ('private'|'team'|'public'), optional archived (missing means false), optional deniedUserIds (missing means empty). Inputs obey these types, except action may be any string. There are no asynchronous operations, clocks, or external services. Use Node 22 JavaScript ESM, node:test and node:assert/strict; no dependencies or network. Run node --test test/*.test.js.
